notes: Google TAG reported that Hermit was used by Italian authorities against targets in Italy, with ISP cooperation in the deployment.
Google TAG reported Hermit deployments in Kazakhstan attributed to government use.

Google TAG reported Predator campaigns targeting users in Egypt; the report does not name the specific purchasing agency, so the government-customer link is reported rather than forensically attributed.
Sekoia's 2025 'Predators for Hire' report lists Egypt among reported Predator customer countries, recounting prior public reporting.
Sekoia's 2025 'Predators for Hire' report lists Greece among reported Predator customer countries, recounting prior public reporting on the Greek surveillance scandal.
Sekoia's 2025 'Predators for Hire' report lists Madagascar among reported Predator customer countries, recounting prior public reporting.
Citizen Lab attributed Pegasus infections of Saudi dissidents, including Omar Abdulaziz, to Saudi-linked operators.
Citizen Lab attributed the Trident exploit targeting Ahmed Mansoor to UAE-linked operators described as 'Stealth Falcon'.
Amnesty's forensic investigations attributed Pegasus targeting of Moroccan journalists, including Omar Radi, to Moroccan authorities.
The Pegasus Project investigation, with Amnesty Security Lab forensic analysis, attributed the targeting of Carine Kanimba to the Rwandan government.
Pegasus Project reporting backed by Amnesty forensics documented Hungarian government use of Pegasus, which Hungarian officials later acknowledged.
Citizen Lab's Project Torogoz investigation found mass Pegasus targeting of journalists and civil society consistent with Salvadoran government use.
Citizen Lab attributed the Predator network-injection operation against presidential candidate Ahmed Eltantawy to the Egyptian government.
Amnesty's Predator Files documented Predator spyware use in Greece, including against journalist Thanasis Koukakis.
Citizen Lab attributed Hacking Team RCS targeting of ESAT journalists to Ethiopian operators.

Meta's December 2021 Threat Report on the Surveillance-for-Hire Industry, as reported by TechCrunch, said Cytrox 'had customers in' Vietnam; Meta removed ~300 Facebook and Instagram accounts linked to Cytrox. Separately, Amnesty's Predator Files (2023) reported evidence of Intellexa product sales to Vietnam's Ministry of Public Security and that Google TAG associated the REPLYSPY Predator campaign with 'a government actor in Vietnam'.
